cands.bio: Mayor of Cape May, NJ, since January 2021 and a member of Cape May City Council for eight years. Holds a bachelor's degree from Mount Saint Mary's University and an MBA from Saint Joseph's University. Describes himself as a small business owner. Democratic nominee for NJ-2.

endorsements.text: Blue Dog PAC endorsed him, according to Wikipedia.
Emgage Action is listed among his endorsements and voter guide recommendations on Ballotpedia.

In his Ballotpedia survey he lists endorsements from Amy Kennedy, Woodstown Mayor Joe Hiles, former Middle Township mayors Susan DeLanzo, Nate Doughty and Michael Clark, former West Cape May Mayor Carol Sabo, Cape May County NAACP Vice President Clayton Palmer, and former Carneys Point Mayor Patrick Bomba (self-reported).

cands.gaps: His birthplace and exact birth year are not confirmed; Wikipedia gives only 1984/1985. We found no record of when or whether he moved to New Jersey beyond his statement that he is a lifelong South Jersey resident. We found no documented actions or statements on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on institutional or foreign land buyers, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun policy, abortion, or school choice. He says he has not raised Cape May taxes in seven years, but we did not find a municipal record confirming it. We found no documented land-use stances on data centers or development, and no reported controversies in the pages reviewed.

qual.background: Cape May City Council member for eight years and mayor since 2021, elected three times. Holds an MBA and says he is a small business owner. As mayor he oversaw construction of a new library, fire house and community center, and a new police station is in progress.
qual.why: Local elected executive experience as mayor and council member puts him in the middle band. He has no legislative experience at the state or federal level and no legal or prosecutorial background.

clean-money.evidence: He says he supports public financing of elections so candidates answer to the people and not to billionaires and corporate PACs. He also backs full transparency in political spending and a ban on members of Congress trading stocks.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: He says he will fight for federal investment in coastal resiliency, wetland and dune restoration, and to preserve South Jersey's beaches, wetlands, farmland and pinelands.

cands.bio: Dentist who ran a South Jersey practice for about 30 years. Dennis Township mayor, Cape May County freeholder, NJ Assemblyman (2002–2008) and State Senator until 2018/2019. U.S. Representative for NJ-2 since 2019, elected as a Democrat and switched to Republican in 2020.

controversies.text: Federal records show $27,900 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; $24,791 from individuals passed through that PAC in 2025-26.
Missed 10 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (1.5%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 2, 2026-04-27 to 2026-04-27.

In December 2020 Van Drew was one of 126 House Republicans on a Supreme Court brief backing Texas's suit to void four states' 2020 results. The Court dismissed that suit for lack of standing. On Jan. 6-7, 2021 he voted to reject Arizona's and Pennsylvania's electoral votes.

endorsements.text: Donald Trump is listed as endorsing Van Drew in the 2026 race. Trump also endorsed him in 2024 and, per Wikipedia, after his 2019 switch to the Republican Party.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions by Van Drew on data centers, homestead property tax elimination, limits on investor or foreign land buying, or school choice and teacher pay. We found nothing on police pay and pensions or penalties for disorder, and no record of a stated clean-money pledge. His current 2026 platform could not be read because his campaign website page held only a sign-up form. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. The Ballotpedia page was cut off partway, so its key-vote and state-legislative sections were not read. Where he spent his childhood before high school is not documented, and neither is the year his family moved to New Jersey.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.
